sections.note: This course introduces students to the rich and diverse cultural heritage of Bulgaria. Through discussions of history, art, folklore, film, and contemporary life, we will explore how Bulgarians express their identity within the context of the Balkans and Europe – at the cultural crossroads between East and West. Special attention will be given to values, behaviors, beliefs, and emotions. The course will include lectures, discussions, films, and interactive sessions. No knowledge of Bulgarian language is required.
sections.title: Intro to Bulgarian Culture

sections.note: Contemporary Autocracy in Theory, Law, and Practice Based on case studies from Russia, Eastern Europe, and Eurasia, this class explores contemporary legal, media, and political practices used by autocratic actors to assert their power. The course analyzes the impact of these practices on the rule of law, human rights and freedoms, sustainable development, and democracy in general, both in the region and globally. It provides a historical overview of the development of autocratic practices, an introduction to its scholarly analysis using concepts from law, philosophy, and politics, and an investigation of specific contemporary examples. The course will be delivered in a seminar format. There are no prerequisites, although familiarity with political context in the region is helpful.
sections.title: Theory, Law, and Practice

sections.note: This course focuses on migrants, refugees, and internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Eurasia, specifically Central Asia and the South Caucasus, with some attention paid to Ukraine as well. The course begins with a historical and socio-cultural overview of Central Asia and the South Caucasus, emphasizing the regions’ transformation from Soviet to post-Soviet. Next, the concepts of migration and forced displacement are introduced from theoretical, legal, and practical perspectives. The remainder of the course is spent discussing case studies of the growing numbers of migrants, refugees, and IDPs across Eurasia. No prior knowledge is required.
sections.title: Migrants, Refugees, & Eurasia
